headline_marked: [[AI Email Agents Are Phishable]] with Social Engineering Attacks, Spilling User Data
headline: AI Email Agents Are Phishable with Social Engineering Attacks, Spilling User Data
summary: Researchers demonstrate that AI email agents like OpenClaw can be tricked into exposing user data using phishing tactics, highlighting a new class of vulnerability.
details: AI email agents, designed to read and act on emails, are now susceptible to social engineering attacks. Researchers have shown that agents like OpenClaw can be manipulated through carefully crafted prompts, similar to phishing attacks targeting humans, leading to the disclosure of sensitive user data.

This vulnerability, known as prompt injection, bypasses traditional security measures. Instead of exploiting technical flaws or memory corruption, attackers use persuasive language, urgency, or impersonation to trick the AI into following malicious instructions embedded within seemingly legitimate content.

The implications are significant, as these agents handle sensitive user information and trigger actions. If an agent can be tricked by a convincing prompt, attackers can potentially gain unauthorized access or control without needing to compromise the underlying server or infrastructure.

Traditional defenses like system prompts, rate limiting, or input length restrictions proved ineffective. System prompt instructions act as soft constraints, easily overridden by sufficiently persuasive adversarial prompts that exploit the AI's reasoning about plausibility.

Content moderation tools and Web Application Firewalls (WAFs) are also ill-equipped to detect this threat, as the malicious payload arrives as legitimate email content and doesn't typically contain known malicious URLs or code.

A new defense layer, Sentinel, has been proposed to sit between the application and the LLM. It uses pattern matching and semantic similarity analysis to detect and neutralize adversarial prompts before they reach the AI agent.

Sentinel employs a two-layer approach: a fast-path regex layer for known prompt injection patterns and a deep-path vector similarity layer that analyzes the semantic meaning of content to identify social engineering tactics.

If a phishing payload is detected, Sentinel can rewrite it to remove the adversarial intent or block the request entirely, preventing the AI agent from executing harmful instructions and protecting user data.

topic: equal ai raises 30m for call screening service
headline_marked: [[Equal AI raises $30M]] to screen calls and manage your conversations
headline: Equal AI raises $30M to screen calls and manage your conversations
summary: The startup's AI assistant handles incoming calls, providing context and quick replies, and has already garnered over a million monthly active users.
details: Equal AI announced today it has secured $30 million in Series B funding, led by Prosus Ventures and Tomales Bay Capital, with participation from Think Investments and Valiant Fund. This brings the company's total funding to over $42 million.

The startup's AI assistant is designed to receive calls on behalf of users, gathering information about the caller's purpose and relaying it to the user. It can also respond to callers with pre-set or custom messages.

Currently available on Android, Equal AI has seen significant traction with over a million monthly active users and 300,000 daily active users since its launch last year. The app supports over 10 languages, including support for code-mixing.

The funding will be used to further develop the AI assistant, with plans to introduce screening for known numbers, proactive actions like texting delivery addresses, an iOS version, and a paid subscription tier.

Founded in 2022 by Keshav Reddy, Equal AI initially focused on data-sharing for financial services but pivoted to the call assistant use case due to the high volume of unsolicited calls consumers receive in India.

The company faces competition from established players like Google and Apple, as well as rivals such as Truecaller and Cloaked, but Prosus Ventures believes Equal AI's understanding of local context provides a competitive edge.
